narration.text: Genesis five reads like a list of funerals. Name after name, the same three words close every life.
And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.
And he died. And he died. Then one line breaks the pattern.
And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
He did not leave his family to find God. He walked with God while raising one, for three hundred years, one ordinary day at a time.
And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.
Notice what the text never gives Enoch: no miracle, no battle, no famous speech. Only a walk. Walking with someone means keeping their pace and their direction, every single day, and that was enough.
Enoch is the first man in the Bible who never dies. His son Methuselah outlives everyone, and his great-grandson is Noah.
This is part six. The full story, from Cain and Abel to the days before the flood, is in the long video on the channel.
